answer.rationale: With the line at 94% of committed volume and no buffer, any supplier transition risk (onboarding, invoicing setup, qualification) could trigger a delivery shortfall that would far outweigh the unit-cost savings from switching. Memory_c2's low-cost vendor switch was recorded as smooth, but that was under different capacity conditions and hasn't been verified against current constraints; I'm choosing to verify memory_c4 instead because renegotiating with the incumbent is the lower-risk lever that has a track record of recovering real margin without disrupting scope or continuity (reinforced by memory_c1's stability record). This won't necessarily hit the full 18% mandate on its own, so I'm flagging that finance's target may require a second sourcing decision next cycle (e.g., second-sourcing or a vetted switch) once there's more slack in the line or more certainty about the low-cost vendor's performance under current volume pressure. Deferring entirely (memory_c5) isn't viable since the contract doesn't auto-renew and expires in 14 days.
